title: Particles: は・が・を・に・で・と・も・の
description: The core case particles: objects, places of action vs. existence, time, means, and question-word subjects.

questions.prompt: わたしは{毎朝|まいあさ}コーヒー（　）{飲|の}みます。
questions.explanation: **を** marks the direct object of an action verb. Coffee is the thing being drunk, so it takes を: コーヒーを飲みます.
notes: に marks destinations, time points and recipients. Coffee is none of these here.
が marks the subject (the one doing or being something). Coffee isn't doing the drinking. が appears with objects only for special predicates like 好き, わかる, ほしい, できる.
で marks the place of an action or the means/tool. コーヒーで飲みます would mean 'drink using coffee'.

questions.prompt: {図書館|としょかん}（　）{勉強|べんきょう}します。
questions.explanation: **で** marks the place where an action happens. Studying is an action, so the library takes で.
notes: へ marks direction of movement and goes with verbs like 行く/来る/帰る, not with 勉強する.
図書館を勉強します would mean 'I study the library' (as a subject).
に marks where something exists (いる/ある) or the destination of movement. 勉強する is an action, not existence or movement, so に doesn't work.

questions.prompt: {日曜日|にちようび}（　）{友達|ともだち}と{映画|えいが}を{見|み}ました。
questions.explanation: Specific time points such as days of the week, dates and clock times take **に**: 日曜日に, 3時に, 5月に. (Relative times like 今日, 明日, 毎日 take no particle.)
notes: で marks the place or means of an action, not a point in time.
が would make Sunday the subject, as if Sunday watched the movie.
を marks the direct object. 映画 is already the object here.
questions.translation: I watched a movie with a friend on Sunday.

questions.prompt: バス（　）{学校|がっこう}へ{行|い}きます。
questions.explanation: **で** marks the means or tool used to do something, including transport: バスで, 電車で, 日本語で, はしで.
notes: と means 'together with (someone)'. バスと行きます would mean you travel with the bus as a companion.
に with vehicles is used with 乗る (バスに乗ります, 'get on the bus'), not with 行く to express the means.
を with 行く marks a route you pass through (道を行く). It doesn't express the means of transport.
questions.translation: I go to school by bus.

questions.prompt: {公園|こうえん}に{猫|ねこ}（　）います。
questions.explanation: In 'there is X' sentences with いる/ある, the thing that exists is marked with **が**, and the location with に: [place]に[thing]がいます.
notes: で marks a place of action. The location is already marked with に, and 猫 isn't a place.
へ marks a direction of movement.
を marks a direct object, but いる doesn't take one.
questions.translation: There is a cat in the park.

questions.prompt: スーパーでパン（　）{卵|たまご}を{買|か}いました。
questions.explanation: **と** joins nouns into a complete list: 'A and B'. (や is used for a non-exhaustive list: 'A, B and so on'.)
notes: へ marks a direction of movement.
が would make the bread the subject that did the buying.
パンで would mean 'using bread' (as a tool). The place is already marked with スーパーで.
questions.translation: I bought bread and eggs at the supermarket.

questions.prompt: リーさんは{学生|がくせい}です。わたし（　）{学生|がくせい}です。
questions.explanation: **も** means 'also/too'. It replaces は, が or を: わたしも学生です = 'I'm a student too'.
notes: を marks the object of an action verb. です isn't an action verb.
の links two nouns (わたしの学生 = 'my student'). It can't connect わたし to です like this.
へ marks a direction of movement.
questions.translation: Lee is a student. I'm a student too.

questions.prompt: {駅|えき}（　）{家|いえ}まで{歩|ある}いて10{分|ぷん}です。
questions.explanation: **から〜まで** means 'from … to/until …'. It works for places (駅から家まで) and for times (9時から5時まで).
notes: まで already marks the end point (家まで). The station is the starting point, so it needs から.
で marks the place of an action or a means. It doesn't express a starting point.
に marks a destination. The station is where you start, not where you go.
questions.translation: It's a ten-minute walk from the station to my house.

questions.prompt: これはだれ（　）{傘|かさ}ですか。
questions.explanation: **の** links two nouns. Here it shows possession: だれの傘 = 'whose umbrella'.
notes: に marks place, time or a recipient. It can't link two nouns into 'whose umbrella'.
が after だれ would make だれ the subject of a predicate, but 傘 is a noun and needs の to connect.
Question words such as だれ, なに and どこ can't take は. The sentence also already has a topic (これは).

questions.explanation: The location of existence (いる/ある) takes **に**: 部屋にだれがいますか.
notes: と means 'with'. 部屋と would mean 'together with the room'.
を marks a direct object, and いる doesn't take one.
で marks where an action happens. Being/existing (いる) is not an action, so the location takes に. (Compare 部屋で勉強します.)

questions.prompt: この{道|みち}（　）まっすぐ{行|い}ってください。
questions.explanation: With movement verbs (行く, 歩く, 渡る, 通る), **を** marks the route or space you move through: 道を行く, 橋を渡る, 公園を散歩する.
notes: に would make the road the destination ('go to the road'). That conflicts with まっすぐ, which describes moving along it.
が would make the road the subject, as if the road itself were going straight.
の links nouns. この道の… would need another noun after it.
questions.translation: Please go straight along this road.

questions.prompt: すみません、{日本語|にほんご}（　）よくわかりません。
questions.explanation: **わかる** marks what is understood with **が**, not を (like 好き, できる, ほしい). (は is also possible for contrast.)
notes: に marks a target or location. It doesn't mark the thing understood.
日本語で would mean 'in Japanese' (as the language used). It doesn't say what you don't understand.
わかる isn't a transitive action verb, so it doesn't take を. 日本語をわかる is a very common learner mistake.
questions.translation: Sorry, I don't really understand Japanese.

questions.prompt: A：だれ（　）{来|き}ましたか。　B：{山田|やまだ}さんが{来|き}ました。
questions.explanation: When a question word is the subject, it must take **が**: だれが, なにが, どれが. The answer keeps が as well: 山田さんが来ました.
notes: だれも with a positive verb isn't used. だれも is used with negatives: だれも来ませんでした = 'nobody came'.
を marks an object, but だれ is the one who came (the subject).
は marks known or given information (the topic), but a question word is unknown by definition. だれは… is ungrammatical.
questions.translation: A: Who came? B: Mr. Yamada came.
